profiles.name: THansen
profiles.profile: The ball-striking showed up, the putter absolutely did not, and that’s the whole picture here: a one-round file where the tee-to-green stuff looked legit while the flatstick drove the bus straight into a ditch. If you’re looking for the identity, it’s simple — hit enough decent shots to keep the card alive, then donate strokes on the greens like they’re a tax write-off. The strange part is the short game helped, which makes the putting tantrum even louder.

profiles.name: doncallan
profiles.tagline: ONE CLUB WAR CRIMES, ONE GREEN MELTDOWN
profiles.profile: This is a mixed bag wrapped in a caution sign. The irons are trying to be useful, but the scoring keeps getting kneecapped by short-game and putting damage, and the result is a guy who can hang around for stretches before the round leaks out through the floorboards. There’s enough on the approach side to keep hope alive, but the rest of the card keeps acting like it forgot what a save is. When the touch and the putter are both sideways, the golf turns into a slow-motion car chase.

profiles.name: bkane
profiles.tagline: BALL STRIKER WITH A BIPOLAR PUTTER
profiles.profile: When this one is on, it looks like somebody finally taught the irons how to bully a golf course. The pattern is pretty clear: massive tee-to-green control, plenty of looks, and enough short-game touch to keep the whole thing from getting weird. The catch is that the scoring can still drift depending on which version of the putter shows up, because there’s a little bit of genius and a little bit of “please stop three-jacking” in the same file. Still, this is the kind of golf that can spit out a low card when the greens stop being rude.

profiles.name: DLudGolf
profiles.tagline: GOLFING LIKE THE PUTTER OWES HIM MONEY
profiles.profile: This dude is basically a one-man demo reel for tee-to-green damage. The long game and short game have both shown enough juice to make the card look obnoxiously clean, and the putter has even joined the party instead of setting the place on fire. The weird part is the net finish keeps refusing to fully cash in on how sharp the ball-striking has been, which makes the profile feel a little cursed, like the math and the leaderboard are in different zip codes. Still, this is good golf hiding behind a mildly petty scoring gremlin.

profiles.name: LeftyMurph
profiles.tagline: ALL THAT APPROACH, THEN THE AXE STOPS SWINGING
profiles.profile: This is a tidy little ball-striking file that never quite turns into a monster because the scoring just doesn’t get mean enough. The irons are doing most of the heavy lifting, the short game gives a little support, and the putter has at least stayed civil. It’s not flashy, but it’s the sort of round shape that keeps you from donating a bunch of strokes to the rest of the field. The ceiling is there if the birdie count wakes up and the occasional clunky hole stops showing up like an unpaid bill.

profiles.name: gbburn
profiles.tagline: WEDGES LOADED, PUTTER OFF THE RAILS
profiles.profile: The short game showed up with a hammer, and the putter answered by trying to set the damn thing on fire. That’s the identity here: enough around-the-green rescue work to suggest the hands can save a mess, but the flatstick spent the round robbing the file of any real momentum. It’s a weirdly spiky profile because the ingredients are not bad at all — a few decent strikes, some touch, some survivable scoring — but the putter made sure it never got pretty. Classic “why is this harder than it should be?” golf.
